sections.body: The Rust API Guidelines are recommendations for the design, documentation, and testing of Rust APIs. They help an API author write an API that is easy to use and hard to misuse. Each guideline carries a stable code (for example C-CONV) and is enforced in practice by Clippy lints.

The Rust Style Guide captures the common style conventions of the Rust community: naming, whitespace, comments, error handling, and more. It is a style reference, not a compiler or linter, and is updated on the nightly documentation.

The Cargo Book documents the Rust build system and package manager. `cargo build` compiles the current package (and its dependencies) for the target platform, writing artifacts under `target/`. Run `cargo <command> --help` for the full option list; the book explains each command, its flags, and their effects.
qualifications: Run `cargo build --help` for the authoritative, version-specific option list.

sections.body: The Rustc Book is a reference for the `rustc` compiler: how to invoke it, its command-line options, and how to read its diagnostics. Because the reference tracks the nightly toolchain, a stable `rustc` may differ from the documented flags.
qualifications: The rustc reference tracks the nightly toolchain; flag behaviour can differ on stable.

sections.body: The Rustup Book documents the Rust toolchain installer: installing, updating, and managing toolchains and components. `rustup show` reports the installed and active toolchains; `rustup update` brings a toolchain current.

The rustfmt Book documents `rustfmt`, the code formatter that ships as a component of the Rust distribution. It lists the options `rustfmt` accepts and how to configure it via a `rustfmt.toml` file. Because rustfmt is a nightly component, its option set can change.
qualifications: rustfmt is a nightly component; its option set can change between releases.

sections.body: The Clippy configuration reference documents the lint groups, individual lint levels, and per-lint options. Clippy is a nightly component, so a specific lint may be added, renamed, or removed between releases; treat an unfamiliar lint as possibly version-dependent.
qualifications: Clippy is a nightly component; a lint may be added or removed between releases.

sections.body: The Rustdoc Book documents `rustdoc`, the documentation generator for Rust. It lists the command-line options that control the generated documentation, from output formats to the HTML template and theme. Because rustdoc tracks the compiler, option behaviour can differ between toolchains.
qualifications: rustdoc tracks the compiler; option behaviour can differ between toolchains.

commands.purpose: Compile the current package, producing its binary or library artifacts.
examples: `cargo build` compiles the current package and writes its artifacts (a binary for a `bin` target, a library for a `lib` target) under `target/`; `cargo build --release` builds an optimized release profile.
prerequisites: A Cargo package or workspace: a manifest (`Cargo.toml`) is present in the working directory or an ancestor of it.
compatibility: Syntax and options are documented for the installed `cargo`; run `cargo build --help` for the version-specific option list. The selection flags `-p`/`--package`, `-w`/`--workspace`, `--target`, and `--features`/`--all-features` choose the package(s), target, and feature set to build; `--offline` resolves from the local cache only and `--locked` asserts the lockfile will not be changed.

`cargo build` does not execute a program, so it has no program-argument forwarding after `--`; compiler flags are supplied through `RUSTFLAGS` or the documented build options rather than a program-argument separator.

effect_notes.detail: produces the final build artifacts (a binary and/or library) under `target/` — the build-output side effect that distinguishes `cargo build` from the check commands.
may download dependencies that are not yet cached; `--offline` (or `--frozen`) prevents any download.

commands.purpose: Compile and run the current package's tests, including the documentation tests (doctests).
examples: `cargo test` compiles and runs the package's unit, integration, and doctests; `cargo test --lib` runs only the library's unit tests and `cargo test --bins` only the binaries' tests.

`cargo test --doc` runs the documentation tests (doctests) only — the doctest-vs-other-tests distinction; a doctest is the fenced code in a `///` or `//!` doc comment that `cargo test --doc` compiles and runs.
prerequisites: A Cargo package or workspace with tests or doctests: a manifest (`Cargo.toml`) is present in the working directory or an ancestor of it.
compatibility: Syntax and options are documented for the installed `cargo`; run `cargo test --help` for the version-specific option list. The selection flags `-p`/`--package`, `-w`/`--workspace`, `--target`, and `--features`/`--all-features` choose the package(s), target, and feature set to test; `--offline` resolves from the local cache only and `--locked` asserts the lockfile will not be changed.

Doctests are the fenced code in doc comments: `cargo test` runs them together with the unit and integration tests, while `cargo test --doc` runs the doctests only. Arguments after `--` are forwarded to the test binary; `--lib`/`--bins`/`--tests`/`--doc` select which target types run.

effect_notes.detail: compiles and runs the package's tests — unit, integration, and doctests execute — the execute side of the family.
may download dependencies that are not yet cached; `--offline` (or `--frozen`) prevents any download.

commands.purpose: Display the active toolchain, the installed toolchains, and the active override for the current directory.
examples: `rustup show` prints the active toolchain (channel, host, release), the installed toolchains, and any directory override in force; `rustup show --active-toolchain` prints only the active toolchain name.
prerequisites: `rustup` is installed (the Rust toolchain installer); the active toolchain is the one the installer selected or pinned for the directory.
compatibility: Syntax and options are documented for the installed `rustup`; run `rustup show --help` for the version-specific option list. The help/version mechanism is `rustup --help`, `rustup --version`, and `rustup show --active-toolchain` (which reports the toolchain name for the current directory).

When the active toolchain's version is unknown or differs from the documented baseline, report the version `rustup show` actually returns rather than assuming a documented version applies; that version-qualification is preserved, not flattened to an unconditional claim. Retrieving this entry is documentation lookup: it surfaces toolchain-inspection guidance and does not change the toolchain; the calling agent decides whether to run `rustup show` through its own terminal tools.
